title: PROFIT // PROPHET
tagline: Both called the crash. Only one got a bonus.
layout: VERTICAL SPLIT: a hard vertical seam down the middle of the poster. Left half: the Wall Street trader screaming at red falling charts, lit cold blue by screens. Right half: the subway platform preacher holding up his cardboard THE END IS NEAR sign, lit warm by a platform lamp. Both raise one arm at the same height so the two halves rhyme across the seam.

title: BRAKE // BREAK
tagline: About four seconds of showtime.
layout: TOP AND BOTTOM SPLIT inside one subway car, a horizontal seam across the middle like the car is cut in two. Top half: the train operator yanking the red emergency brake, sparks streaking past the window. Bottom half: the breakdancer in a one handed freeze on the floor of the same car, upside down so his pose mirrors the operator's arm. The poles run straight through both halves.

title: TAWK // TOCK
tagline: Say it like a New Yorker. It's the same word.
layout: NOIR, ONE SCENE TWO READINGS: the great four faced golden clock over the Grand Central information booth fills the upper two thirds, glowing, beams of light through the windows. Below it, a man in a car in the rain shouting into his phone, his breath fogging the windshield, the clock's light falling on him. The clock's face and the man's open mouth line up on the same vertical axis.

title: KNEW // NEW
tagline: One knew it when. One just got here.
layout: BACK TO BACK: the old timer in a flat cap and the new transplant with a giant rolling suitcase sit back to back on the same park bench, facing opposite edges of the poster. Behind the old timer the block is painted as it was decades ago in sepia; behind the newcomer the same block is glass towers in bright colour. The split runs through the bench.

title: MINER // MINOR
tagline: One digs the tunnel. One is digging himself a hole.
layout: CROSS SECTION, ABOVE AND BELOW GROUND: a cutaway of a New York street. The lower two thirds is the underground: a sandhog in a hard hat with a headlamp beside a giant tunnel boring machine, rock and pipes. The top third is the sidewalk at night: a nervous teenager holding a fake ID up to a huge bouncer outside a bar. The sidewalk slab is the seam.

title: IDLE // IDOL
tagline: One gets reported. One gets screamed at.
layout: MIRROR SPLIT, DIAGONAL: a diagonal seam from top right to bottom left. Upper left: a yellow cab idling at a curb with exhaust curling into the air, its driver asleep at the wheel. Lower right: a screaming K pop fan with a glowing lightstick in a stadium crowd, confetti. The exhaust from the cab turns into the confetti across the seam.

title: MORNING // MOURNING
tagline: Bacon egg and cheese. Then one day the gate stays down.
layout: SAME PLACE, TWO TIMES: one bodega storefront, split down the middle. Left half: 7am, door open, a bacon egg and cheese handed out in foil, sunlight, the deli cat on the counter. Right half: the same storefront at night, the metal gate pulled down and covered in flowers, candles and taped photographs, the deli cat in the window. The storefront lines continue across the seam exactly.

title: CAH // CAW
tagline: Pahk the cah. The crow has opinions.
layout: ONE SCENE, LOW ANGLE COMEDY: a huge crow standing on the hood of a parked car fills the frame, beak wide open mid CAW, feathers ruffled. Behind the windshield, through the glass, the car's owner holds a parking ticket with both hands on his head. A street sweeper passes in the background. The crow and the man are the two halves of one joke.

title: PEACE // PIECE
tagline: Give one a chance. Fold the other in half.
layout: VERTICAL SPLIT WITH A RHYME: left half, a barefoot hippie with a guitar on a mosaic in Central Park holding up two fingers in a peace sign; right half, a pizza man holding up a single folded slice at the same height and angle as the peace sign, cheese stretching across the seam into the other half.

title: HEARD // HERD
tagline: You heard? The herd heard.
layout: TOP SMALL, BOTTOM HUGE: the top third is an intimate close moment, two hairdressers in a salon leaning in to whisper, foil in a customer's hair. The bottom two thirds is an enormous herd of commuters stampeding up the escalators at Penn Station at rush hour, seen from above, all of them turning their flower heads toward the whisper.

title: ONE // WON
tagline: Scratch one. Win one.
layout: THE TICKET: the whole poster is designed like a giant scratch off lottery ticket, gold foil border. In the middle, the silver scratch layer is half scratched away by a coin held in a hand: under the silver on the left a man scratching at a bodega counter, revealed on the right the same man leaping in the air outside the bodega with confetti. The scratched silver flakes drift across.

title: SON // SUN
tagline: You know what it is, son. Twice a year, it's the sun.
layout: MANHATTANHENGE: the sun sets dead centre at the end of 42nd Street between the skyscrapers, a golden canyon of light. In the foreground, silhouetted against it, a father and his son on a stoop, the father's hand on the boy's shoulder, both turned toward the sun. The long shadows of the two run toward the viewer.

title: PAIR // PEAR
tagline: One costs four hundred dollars. One is lonelier.
layout: SHRINE AND STILL LIFE: the top two thirds is a sneaker boutique lit like a cathedral, a sneakerhead on his knees holding up one perfect pair of sneakers to the spotlight like a relic. The bottom third is a bodega counter where one single green pear sits under a buzzing fluorescent tube, the bodega guy and the deli cat staring at it with the same reverence. The beams of light from above fall on both.

title: MADE // MAID
tagline: One got made. One made the bed.
layout: HOTEL CORRIDOR, BOTH ENDS: one long grand hotel corridor in one point perspective. In the foreground a made guy in a sharp pinstripe suit with a pinky ring, leaning on the wall, a toothpick. At the far end of the same corridor, small and lit by a chandelier, a hotel maid folds a towel into a swan on her cart. The carpet pattern leads the eye from one to the other.

title: MAIL // MALE
tagline: Neither rain nor sleet. Neither shirt nor pants.
layout: BILLBOARD ABOVE, STREET BELOW: the top half is a giant SoHo billboard of a male model in underwear smouldering, a pigeon sitting on the billboard edge. The bottom half is the street under it in a downpour, a mail carrier in blue shorts with his umbrella flipped inside out, mailbag soaked, looking up at the billboard in disbelief.

title: IN // INN
tagline: One decides who gets in. One takes anybody for forty dollars.
layout: SPLIT BY A VELVET ROPE: a velvet rope runs diagonally across the poster. Above the rope, a giant bouncer with a clipboard at a neon nightclub door at 1am, the line of hopefuls. Below the rope, a tiny warm hostel lobby where a sleepy clerk hands a giant wooden key tag to a backpacker, a cat asleep on the desk.

title: BARE // BEAR
tagline: Same street. Different market.
layout: TIMES SQUARE FACE OFF: the street performer in nothing but a hat, boots and a guitar stands on the left, and on the right a stock trader in a full brown bear costume holding a briefcase, both under the blazing billboards, facing each other like a western showdown, tourists photographing both. The red ticker of falling numbers wraps the buildings.

title: HAIR // HARE
tagline: One cuts it. One pulls it out of a hat.
layout: MIRROR TRICK: a barbershop mirror fills the poster. In front, from behind, a Bushwick barber gives a fresh fade, clippers buzzing. In the mirror's reflection, instead of the barbershop, a street magician in Washington Square Park pulls a huge white rabbit out of a top hat, the arch behind him, a crowd gasping.

title: PEAK // PEEK
tagline: Best view in the city. Second best view in the city.
layout: THROUGH THE PEEPHOLE: the poster is framed as the round fisheye view through an apartment door peephole: inside the circle, the top of the Empire State Building observation deck at sunset with the whole city glowing. Outside the circle, the dark wood of the door and, pressed up close, the giant eye of a nosy neighbour in a housecoat and curlers peering in.

title: RIGHT // WRITE
tagline: You can't turn right on red. He can't write on deadline.
layout: INTERSECTION FROM ABOVE: a high overhead view of a Manhattan intersection at night. A yellow cab is stuck at a red light with a huge NO TURN ON RED sign, the driver's arms out the window. On the corner a café window glows, and inside a writer slumped over a laptop surrounded by crumpled pages. The crosswalk stripes run between them like lines on a page.

title: NOSE // KNOWS
tagline: One smells trouble. One knows your order.
layout: BOTH SIDES OF A COUNTER: a bodega counter splits the poster horizontally. On the customer side, a commuter sniffing the air suspiciously, eyes narrowed. On the other side the bodega guy already sliding over a bacon egg and cheese on a roll before a word was said, egg sizzling on the grill, the cat on the counter between them.

title: BERRY // BURY
tagline: Same farm stand energy. Very different harvest.
layout: SEASONS SPLIT: a vertical seam down the middle. Left: the Union Square Greenmarket in bright morning sun, a farmer holding a basket of strawberries and blueberries. Right: dusk on a hill in Green-Wood Cemetery, a gravedigger leaning on his shovel among old angel statues, the Manhattan skyline far behind. The basket and the shovel are held at the same height.

title: BLEW // BLUE
tagline: He blew it. She bleeds blue.
layout: THE BALLPARK, TWO MOODS: the top of the poster is the mound, a closer with his head buried in his glove after blowing the save, the scoreboard glowing. The bottom is the stands, a die hard fan in head to toe blue and orange, face painted, roaring with a giant foam finger, absolutely undefeated. Rain and confetti fall on both.

title: DEAR // DEER
tagline: What can I get you, dear? Staten Island has an answer.
layout: DELI WINDOW, SUBURBAN STREET: the inside of a deli counter fills the bottom half, a deli lady handing over a sandwich with a smile, calling everybody dear. Through the big deli window behind her, the top half shows a Staten Island cul de sac at dawn where a family of deer stand calmly in the street while a man in a bathrobe stares at them, newspaper in hand.
